solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leave drink, taking in small talk

indicators.note: the two words before it close around the next piece, holding it between them

parts.note: to leave is to go
a sip is a small drink
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their drink while overhearing idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small talk' reads as one phrase, but 'small' is a separate abbreviation and only 'talk' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter about other people is a kind of talk, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lies low, forced to cover lake and fuel sources

indicators.note: the rearranged words go around the lake letter
forced suggests the words are pushed into a new shape

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone lies low, made to hide a lake and sources of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges LIES LOW, and 'to cover' puts that around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts drilled to extract petroleum supply fuel, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Odd items perhaps of washing hung out — here's why?

definitions.meaning: miscellaneous small items, as in sundry odds and ends
split 3,5 it says the ... the washing on the line

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: the sun dries the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous odds and ends are grouped under this plural noun.

clue.text: Post Office worker pockets black book that's an earner

indicators.note: the worker takes the black letter inside, as into a pocket

parts.note: a toiler is someone who works hard
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A postal worker hides a black book that makes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap novel written mainly to make money, idiomatically to keep the pot boiling.

clue.text: Irregular role at home around South America

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

indicators.note: the home word wraps itself about the continent's abbreviation

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: An actor plays an unconventional part while staying home near South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' is a noun here: an irregular soldier, a guerrilla, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla fighter outside the regular army is called an irregular, a military sense.

clue.text: Excitedly contact speaker, importing fine sweets

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the fine abbreviation
excitedly suggests the letters jumble about

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly calls a speaker who brings in fine confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' rearranges CONTACT and SPEAKER together, and 'importing' takes F into the mix. Pontefract cakes are British liquorice sweets from Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Small black liquorice discs from a Yorkshire town are confectionery, an example of sweets.

clue.text: Bound to include everybody, agreed

indicators.note: the bound word takes everybody inside itself

parts.note: something bound is tied
everybody is all

explanation.surface: Bound to include everyone in the agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that tallied matched each other, a sense of corresponding.

clue.text: Rebellious youth almost broke the boss

indicators.note: the broke word loses its final letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: A rebellious young man is nearly penniless and the head of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for penniless; 'almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed member of a youth subculture, a type of rebellious youth.

clue.text: Made enquiries on one case of vehicle's sudden fall

parts.note: to nose around is to make enquiries
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the outer letters of the vehicle form a casing around it

explanation.surface: Detectives made enquiries into a car's sudden plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the outside letters of 'vehicle', V and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane diving steeply, or prices dropping sharply, is a sudden fall.

clue.text: Time working on board getting marine life forms

indicators.note: on here sends time and working after the board, placed upon it

parts.note: a plank is a long board of wood
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Spending time on a wooden board while studying sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person working on a board; 'on' instead orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms of the sea collectively make up this biological group.

clue.text: Schemes incorporating island's flat areas

indicators.note: the schemes word takes the island letter into its body

parts.note: schemes are plans
I is the usual abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Development schemes for an island include its flat lowlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide expanses of level grassland are a geographical synonym.

clue.text: Fellow listener a few dread

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
the ear is the organ of listening
a few means some

explanation.surface: A fellow listening in feels a few anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dread' is an adjective here, as in 'a dread sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, dread means terrifying, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Hoped to see West End cast

parts.note: W1 is the London postcode for the West End, with the 1 read as the letter I
to cast skin, as a snake does, is to shed it

explanation.surface: Someone had high hopes of seeing a London theatre show's company.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is the postal district of London's West End theatre area; the figure 1 stands for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped for something is to have longed for it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Expanded by serving lager in terminal

indicators.note: the shuffled beer letters go inside the terminal word

parts.note: a terminal point is an end

indicators.note: serving suggests the beer is dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Drinking lager at the station terminal has made someone grow larger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' rearranges the beer's letters into LARGE before 'in' places them in the terminal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made bigger has grown in size, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Strange — credit is short in support of German war machine

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: the Enigma machine encoded German messages in WWII

indicators.note: the credit word loses its last letter

parts.note: to buy on tick is to buy on credit

explanation.surface: Puzzling claim: credit is limited to back the German war effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit; 'short' cuts TICK to TIC, which goes under ENIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious and hard to fathom is puzzling, a synonym of strange.

clue.text: She gets disheartened during American functions

indicators.note: the outer letters of the pronoun sit within the American abbreviation
losing its heart, the pronoun keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman loses heart while attending American social functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' drops the middle letter H of the pronoun before 'during' places what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposes or applications of a thing are its functions, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Poorly grounded person not expected to win

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A poorly grounded person is unlikely to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor tipped to lose is an outsider, the sporting sense.

clue.text: Auditor of former dictator and heir oddly disappearing

parts.note: ex means former
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of heir vanish, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An auditor checks the accounts of an ex-dictator and his vanishing heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly disappearing' removes H and I, the 1st and 3rd letters of HEIR, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who checks accounts or tests candidates is an inspector, as an auditor does.

clue.text: Why some did less?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question asking for the reason certain people achieved less.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: why did some do less? Because they were lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The question 'Why?' is answered by laziness; the clue invites the reason as the answer.

clue.text: Posted popular class edition

parts.note: something popular is in
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A popular class edition was sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' means 'kept up to date', as in 'keep me posted', not sent by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept posted means being kept up to date, an idiom for knowledgeable.

clue.text: Rising stink contained by West Coast city that is a feature of North America

indicators.note: the reversed stink sits inside the city and the abbreviation together

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles on the US West Coast
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: reek means stink

explanation.surface: A rising stench in a West Coast city is a North American feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the stink word upwards in this down entry, and 'contained by' sets it between the city and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Great Lakes is a geographical feature of the continent.

clue.text: Story about Right creates a state of conflict

indicators.note: the story word goes around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a story is a piece of fiction

explanation.surface: A tale about the political Right stirs up discord.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is disagreement or tension, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Showy display from cool and distant European

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it
far means distant

explanation.surface: A showy display from a cool and aloof European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is a verb here: to fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet flourish or an ostentatious fuss counts as a showy display.

clue.text: Creature's show of hesitation in front of pit

indicators.note: the hesitation sound comes first, before the pit

parts.note: er is the sound people make when hesitating
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An animal hesitates at the edge of a deep hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Creature' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat in its white winter coat is an animal, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Person lacking rank — one arriving around beginning of week

indicators.note: the arriving person wraps itself about the start of the week

parts.note: one who comes is a comer
Mon, short for Monday, begins the working week

explanation.surface: A newcomer turns up around Monday morning without any title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning of week' is not the letter W but MON, the abbreviation for Monday, the week's first working day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a noble title is an ordinary citizen, the class sense of the word.

clue.text: Superficial impression made on a student of teeth

parts.note: a dent is a shallow mark pressed into a surface
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A small dent was left on the work of a dentistry student.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plates worn by British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to teeth, as in a check-up at the dentist.

clue.text: What identifies quality of target by hawk?

indicators.note: the target goes beside the bird, following it

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey, loosely a hawk
a mark is a target to aim at

explanation.surface: A question about how to judge a hawk's aim at its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kitemark is the British Standards Institution's quality symbol on UK products.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Standards symbol certifies that a product meets a recognised standard.

clue.text: Clothes and weapon hidden in loo

indicators.note: the weapon is placed inside the word for the toilet

parts.note: the gents is a British name for a men's toilet
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Clothing and a gun stashed in a public lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' is a container here, not a hidden-word signal. The gents is British slang for a men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Items of clothing, plural, match the plural definition directly.

clue.text: Company director's first German buffer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the director is taken

explanation.surface: A firm's director is first of all an elderly German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffer' is British slang for a fusty old man, not a cushioning device.
explanation.definitionFit: An old buffer is a slightly comic elderly man, an informal synonym.
